title: Bezos-led consortium acquires 38% stake in Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group
dek: A consortium led by British businessman Amit Bhatia and including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin acquired 38% of Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group. The group holds an option to buy a controlling stake within 12 months, though without formal commitment.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: 1892 Holdings, led by Amit Bhatia and including Bezos and Saverin, bought 38% of Liverpool from FSG.
bottom_line: Watch for regulatory approval of Bhatia's appointment and any signals about the consortium's intention to exercise the 12-month option for controlling ownership. FSG's stated rationale for the sale and any conditions beyond the option window will clarify the long-term trajectory of the club's ownership.
body: A consortium led by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia and including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and billionaire Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin acquired approximately 38% of Liverpool FC from Fenway Sports Group, according to BBC Sport reporting. The group, named 1892 Holdings after Liverpool's founding year, struck a definitive agreement for what FSG described as a strategic minority investment.

Bhatia will become Liverpool's vice-chairman and join an expanded board pending regulatory approval. Bhatia is the son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal and spent 18 years as a director and co-owner of Queens Park Rangers before relinquishing his stake in that club last month.

The deal is understood to value Liverpool between 5 billion and 6 billion pounds in total, per BBC Sport. The consortium holds an option to acquire a controlling stake within the next 12 months, though that option does not involve a formal commitment to proceed, creating uncertainty about whether majority ownership will shift.

Fenway Sports Group confirmed entering into the definitive agreement for the sale, marking a significant moment in the club's ownership structure after more than a decade under FSG control. The regulatory approval timeline for Bhatia's board appointment remains unclear from the available reporting.
